newsitem.title: GERMANY: German sugar firms plan post-merge investment east.
newsitem.headline: German sugar firms plan post-merge investment east.

text.p: Four northern German sugar firms currently discussing merger plans for later this year would use their combined power to invest in eastern European sugar production, a Zuckerverbund Nord (ZVN) spokesman said.

Singling this out among a number of planned initiatives, he said, "We plan to use our expertise in sugar to strengthen our core business by taking stakes in eastern European companies that are coming up for privatisation."
The spokesman was answering an inquiry after the four companies in a statement said they had reached a general consensus to push through their merger bid by the end of 1997.
He said cost savings would enable the envisaged new company, Nordzucker AG, to invest in eastern European plantings and harvest technology, using its expertise.
But he saw no change in sugar trade flows from that region into the European Union because of potentially strong local demand and long transition periods on the way to EU accession.
Nordzucker AG, if backed by shareholders meetings in September, would account for 30-35 percent of Germany's 26 million tonnes annual sugarbeet output.

It would be owned by shareholders recruited from among some 20,000-23,000 sugar farmers in northern Germany who currently are tied suppliers to ZVN, Union-Zucker Suedhannover GmbH, Zuckerfabrik Harsum AG and Zucker AG Uelzen-Braunschweig.
Mannheim-based European market leader Suedzucker AG accounts for 40-45 percent of German output.
